title: Recycle handoff at the WCLI-53 / WCLI-14 boundary
description:
Written to order by the orchestrator recycle notice of 2026-09-29 ~15:40Z, which asked for a handoff AFTER the request rather than the one WCLI-55/WCLI-56 already carried. Every ref below was read back from the remote or the tracker on this branch, not remembered.

STATE AT HANDOVER, read live. origin/main == origin/dev == e545394 (asserted by rev-list count 0 and an empty tree diff after the last promotion). 0 open PRs. Tree clean, branch dev, nothing unpushed. Tracker: WCLI-52 Done, WCLI-53 Done, WCLI-57 To Do (filed this session), WCLI-14 To Do and unassigned; NOTHING In Progress (quest task list --status "In Progress" with scope.otherRefsRead true and unseenTaskIds empty).

WHAT THIS SESSION LANDED, in opum-ai/ward-cli.
- WCLI-52, PR #110, squash e08c848. runBackup parses the state document after store.read and before the KDF, seal and files.create, so a vault whose document decrypts and does not parse answers vault_state_malformed (or vault_format_unsupported for a stored approval whose snapshot version this build does not implement) and no file is created; before, it backed up with exit 0 and a file ward restore refused, under text promising recovery from a damaged vault. ADR 0010 consequences bullet updated with the decision and its cost (preserving a damaged vault bytes means copying the vault file, not taking a Ward backup). Decision ruled by opum-agent as component design belonging to this repository, so it is recorded here and not in opum-doc.
- WCLI-53, PR #112, squash e545394. test/support/immediate-timers.ts replaces setTimeout with one that fires as a microtask and records the delay; the provider-bound and unresponsive-store tests assert the bound the code applied plus the refusal, with a 1 s ceiling beside them. setup.test.ts old 5 s ceiling equalled Bun default test timeout, so it could only race the harness. The FIFO and vault-busy bounds stay wall-clock with measured margins (0-1 ms; 67-76 ms against a 50 ms busy timeout) and the vault-busy case gained a floor, which catches an unapplied busy timeout (measured: PRAGMA busy_timeout = 0 leaves the code vault_busy at 0.304 ms and the floor reddens).
- Two promotions on the orchestrator instruction: PR #111 (dev to main at e08c848) and PR #113 (at e545394), both landed with git push origin origin/dev:main and verified by ref; main has no rules and no required checks, so those are "no checks configured", not checks passed.
- WCLI-57 filed: a push to dev runs both CI workflows for one SHA and their concurrency groups differ, so the two jobs do not cancel and the contended one is what stretched the bound in the first place. That is the configuration half WCLI-53 deliberately left open. I did not decide it.

SUCCESSOR NEXT WORK: none assigned. The orchestrator was told the queue (WCLI-52, WCLI-53) is complete and asked which to take next, recommending WCLI-14 (the WCLI-50 scope note says the skill and plugin skeleton already exist, so extend rather than re-create) with WCLI-57 second. Do not start ahead of that brief.

NOT TO RE-DERIVE, each paid for this session.
- Component design is this repository own call: cross-repo design is the operator own (ODOC-OP-11), so a design question here is decided and recorded locally, and the orchestrator only needs telling that it was.
- Any new bound test uses test/support/immediate-timers.ts and asserts the delay the code was given; wrap only a fixture that cannot settle, because the fake wins the race against a fast success. A ceiling alone cannot see latency added outside globalThis.setTimeout, which is why the 1 s ceiling sits beside the assertions (measured band: 1.5 s of added latency fails it, 600 ms does not).
- The vault-busy floor (waited >= 50 ms) is the one wall-clock assertion shape that cannot flake: contention only lengthens a lock wait.
- The independent review pattern that worked twice: dispatch opum-workflow reviewer against the pushed head, reproduce every finding before acting, then have the same agent verify the fixes. Both rounds found real defects (a vacuous assertion; a dropped upper bound).
- A citation by line number goes stale when a diff above it shifts the file: WCLI-52 diff moved the FIFO bound from backup.test.ts:538 to :731. Name sites by what they assert.
- This clone remote is HTTPS, so the SSH transport failure opum-agent reported at about 14:53Z is not machine-wide for this repository; reported to them.

OPEN OBLIGATIONS. WCLI-57 is unassigned and tracks the CI overlap. WCLI-14, WCLI-15, WCLI-12, WCLI-21, WCLI-22, WCLI-29, WCLI-33, WCLI-34, WCLI-37, WCLI-38, WCLI-46, WCLI-19, WCLI-30 are To Do and none is this session own. Nothing is blocked, and no decision is pending with the operator.
finalSummary: The durable half of the WCLI-53 / WCLI-14 recycle boundary, written after the orchestrator recycle notice so the successor cursor and this record both postdate the request. It states the live refs (origin/main == origin/dev == e545394, 0 open PRs, nothing In Progress), what the session landed (WCLI-52 in opum-ai/ward-cli#110, WCLI-53 in opum-ai/ward-cli#112, both promoted to main via #111 and #113), WCLI-57 filed for the CI overlap, the not-to-re-derive list from both tasks, and the successor queue with WCLI-14 recommended and WCLI-57 second. The cursor is machine-local and gitignored, so this record is what survives; the flush wrote no tracker note, correctly, because no task was In Progress when it ran. Closed by the same pull request that lands it.
